question: Does a time link that is forced retained/cut among all EXACT minimum-segment partitions remain so when each animal-season source group is allowed one or two extra cuts beyond its minimum? Separate locally impossible time pairs from minimum-objective artifacts.
time_rule: One shared assignment of integer-second observation instants per contiguous segment, positive 1..45000-second gaps. Keep source-blind T0 lower/upper/DBF row-ordinal ordering, no synthetic date-only timestamp imputation, no DST assertion as author truth.

partition_budget.definition: At budget delta, allow ANY feasible contiguous segmentation of that group with cut count <= minimum cut count + delta. Minimum cut count measured separately for each source group and world. Additional cuts are OPTIONAL; no exact-budget forced increases.

classification.mandatory_cut: Every within-budget partition cuts the adjacent link.
classification.mandatory_retain: Every within-budget partition retains the adjacent link.
classification.optional: At least one within-budget partition cuts and at least one retains.

partition_budget.algorithm: Enumerate feasible segment DAG i->j. Shortest prefix and suffix segment counts d0, dn; minimum segments S=d0[N]. For any internal boundary k, min segments of a partition cutting k = d0[k]+dn[k]. Minimum segments retaining link k = min_{i<k<j feasible block} d0[i]+1+dn[j]. A state allowed if cost <=S+delta. Classify using boolean feasibility of each state, do not assume which greedy solution is chosen.
partition_budget.theorem_to_validate: For arbitrary nonempty time-window unions and hereditary contiguous block feasibility, delta>=1 guarantees every link can be cut in some allowed partition; any pairwise-feasible link can be retained in some partition with at most one more cut than optimal by isolating its two records. Thus with delta=1 mandatory retention=0 and mandatory cuts are exactly locally infeasible pairs; delta=2 cannot alter these classifications. This is a mathematical theorem under the declared segment objective, not a biological source claim.
